description: Tests whether combining two independently-motivated levers -- 'compound' items that open 2-4 Charter terms simultaneously (PR #6's best-scoring design, which resists a single-option-name blacklist since every opened axis must be resolved) and 'low cue' restatement (PR #10's hypothesis that pasting the full Charter table inflates the control arm's Charter-choice rate, since an untrained model can just read it) -- compounds into a stronger discrimination signal than either lever alone. The star family, compound_low_cue, builds ~180 scored identifying items at cue level 0-1 combining 2-4 simultaneous rule terms per item, plus a small matched cue-4 sibling pool (unscored, tagged) for later comparison. A dedicated cross_axis_dependency sub-family targets R11 specifically, whose condition (lot seal) is itself a decision axis rather than a fixed run condition -- the Charter-conforming joint plan can require sacrificing money on one axis to keep another legal, which is a deeper cross-field integration test than any single-axis conflict. All other canonical families are covered at supporting scale so criteria_coverage has material across the guide's full playbook.
